correctness.rationale: The classical odd distortion and quadratic Schwarz lemma give the stated radial envelope. Equality at a positive radius makes every pointwise step exact. Comparing the third odd coefficient via the odd square-root Koebe transform gives phi=z/(1-z^2), and equality phases force epsilon=-1, omega=kz^2, f=H+conj(G). For every k>0 its upper boundary slit values have ReG(e^{it})<0 while lower/right mirrored boundary values have opposite signs. Strict monotonicity in the conformal psi-coordinate and divergence at horizontal infinities produce two exact preimages of iy for every y>1/2. The original normalized univalent class is compact and closed under the analytic-phase condition, so the best bound is attained but cannot equal the envelope. At k=0 the analytic Koebe square-root attains equality.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary paper asserts the envelope is sharp for the odd globally univalent class. Its inspected full relevant text does not separate formal local equality from global univalence or prove the strict best-constant inequality for all positive k and r. The earlier 2024 odd-harmonic paper concerns the opposite direction-convex shear and Hardy/coefficient bounds. Actual research-record and literature searches for equality, opposite-shear collisions, and the strict sharpness gap did not find implication-equivalent results.

value.rationale: The exact sharpness of a radial growth theorem is a central geometric invariant, and global injectivity is essential rather than a technical side condition in harmonic shears. This finding gives a complete all-parameter classification of which local analytic envelopes remain sharp under global univalence, constructs actual multiple preimages of the sole formal equality maps, and proves an attained strict best-constant gap via compactness. It resolves a substantive extremizer-compatibility issue left by a recent theorem rather than deriving an arbitrary specialization or presenting a mere numerical negative check.
